prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

</profile>

TEXT_D:
Summary of key policies and commitments (ideological framing removed)

Economy, tax, pensions, childcare
- Cut employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish main rate of self-employed NI by end of Parliament; no rises in income tax or VAT rates stated.
- Triple Lock Plus: uprate State Pension and pensioners’ personal allowance by the highest of inflation, earnings or 2.5%; no new pension taxes; maintain existing pensioner benefits.
- Childcare: 30 hours free for eligible parents from 9 months to school by Sept 2025; nationwide wraparound childcare by Sept 2026.
- Child Benefit based on household income: taper from £120,000 to £160,000.

Work, welfare, carers
- Reform PIP to target genuine needs; expand mental health support; simplify assessments for severe conditions.
- Tighten Work Capability Assessment from Sept 2025; overhaul fit notes to specialist-led.
- Tougher sanctions after 12 months; complete Universal Credit rollout; new Fraud Bill giving DWP HMRC-like powers.
- Continue support for unpaid carers.

Business, SMEs, infrastructure, innovation, trade
- Keep corporation tax; maintain/extend full expensing (to leasing when affordable); SME plan (business rates support, prompt payment enforcement, Open Finance, VAT threshold review, Invest in Women Fund £250m).
- Reallocate £36bn HS2 phase 2 savings to regional transport; nationwide gigabit by 2030; standalone 5G in all populated areas; automated vehicles framework; aviation SAF mandate and revenue support.
- Public R&D to £22bn/yr; >£1.5bn for compute; £4.5bn advanced manufacturing.
- Pursue FTAs (India, GCC); implement CPTPP; maintain TCA with EU while protecting sovereignty claims.

Borders, immigration
- Legal annual cap on work and family visas, falling each year and voted by Parliament.
- Health checks pre-travel; higher Immigration Health Surcharge/insurance where needed; raise Skilled Worker thresholds with inflation.
- Rwanda removals with monthly flights; clear asylum claims in 6 months; more returns deals; seek international asylum rule changes; cap for safe/legal routes set by Parliament.

Defence, security, foreign policy, veterans
- Defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; £10bn munitions; 5% of defence budget for R&D (+2% exploitation); National Defence and Resilience Plan; continued support to Ukraine.
- Veterans Bill; maintain Office for Veterans’ Affairs; visa fee waivers for Commonwealth dependants; benefits disregard for war compensation.

NHS and social care
- NHS funding to rise above inflation annually; recruit 92,000 nurses and 28,000 doctors; expand Pharmacy First; 250 GP surgeries; 50 more CDCs; 40 hospitals by 2030.
- Dental plan: 2.5m extra appointments; service requirement for new dentists; rural incentives.
- Patient choice across providers; NHS tech £3.4bn (App, AI, data platform); cut 5,500 managers; Major Conditions Strategy; Tobacco and Vapes Bill; women’s health measures.
- Mental health: school/college teams to 100% by 2030; early support hubs in every community; expand talking therapies by 50%.

Education, skills, youth
- Mandatory National Service at 18 (full-time military/cyber placements or part-time civic service).
- 100,000 additional apprenticeships funded by closing low-outcome degree courses.
- Ban mobile phones during school day; Advanced British Standard for 16–19; 60,000 more SEN places and 15 special free schools.

Policing, justice, protests
- 8,000 extra neighbourhood police; hotspot policing; Martyn’s Law; tougher sentencing (violent/sexual offences, domestic homicides); four new prisons; expand FNO removals; anti-fraud measures.
- New protest powers: restrict face coverings/pyrotechnics; consider cumulative impact; ban protests outside schools.

Energy, net zero, bills
- Annual North Sea oil and gas licensing; new gas plants; treble offshore wind; first CCS clusters; approve two SMR fleets within 100 days; new nuclear at Wylfa; halve approval times; windfall tax to 2028–29 (subject to prices).
- Bills: maintain price cap; review standing charges; PumpWatch; local electricity markets; £6bn for efficiency plus universal voucher scheme; consent-led onshore wind; solar prioritised on brownfield/roofs; fracking moratorium; import carbon pricing by 2027; UK supply chain bonus in offshore wind.

Housing
- 1.6m homes; lift nutrient neutrality via mitigation fees; fast-track brownfield; densify cities (esp. London); development corporations; protect Green Belt.
- Support buyers: permanent FTB Stamp Duty threshold £425k; new Help to Buy; Mortgage Guarantee continued.
- Leasehold reform (cap ground rents; curb forfeiture; expand commonhold); Renters Reform Bill (abolish Section 21 after court reforms); 2-year CGT relief for landlords selling to tenants.

Communities, transport, drivers
- £20m endowments for 135 towns; extend Shared Prosperity Fund three years; more Freeports/Investment Zones.
- Backing Drivers Bill: no road pricing; reverse London ULEZ expansion; local referendums on LTNs/20mph; extend £2 bus fare cap for the Parliament; Rail Reform Bill to create Great British Railways; nationwide PAYG contactless; parking/pay reforms.

Law, equality, gender
- Clarify Equality Act: sex = biological sex; one legal sex; implement Cass Review; NHS single-sex care rights; parental rights to see curriculum materials.

Rural, farming, fishing, environment, sport, culture
- Farming budget +£1bn over Parliament (inflation-linked); legal food security target and index; fast-track farm infrastructure; five-year tapered seasonal visas; replicate £100m Seafood Fund.
- Plan for Water (tougher penalties, river restoration fund, regulatory reform); maintain record flood defence funding; tree/peat commitments; new National Park; tougher waste crime; prevent new incinerators not yet substantially built.
- Continue grassroots sports facilities funding; independent football regulator; maintain competitive creative tax reliefs; BBC funding review and new complaints process.

Union and devolution
- Extend Shared Prosperity and towns funds UK-wide; protect internal market; specific nation projects on transport, energy and industry; comparable data on public service performance.

TEXT_A:
Summary of key proposals (Green Party Manifesto 2024)

Health and social care
- NHS: Additional revenue £8bn in year one, rising to £28bn by 2030; capital £20bn over five years. Targets include faster GP access, guaranteed NHS dentistry, reduced waiting lists, primary care funding rising by £1.5bn by 2030, £2bn primary care capital, restore public health budgets (+£1.5bn). New NHS dentist contract and funding rising to £3bn/yr by 2030. Pay restoration for staff. National Cancer Plan. Mental health: access to therapies within 28 days; counsellor in every school/college. Support assisted dying with safeguards. End new HIV cases by 2030.
- Social care: Free personal care; workforce pay/career structure; £20bn/yr investment. End exploitation in care visas; right to an essential Care Supporter. Disability: benefits +5%, reforms to assessments; SEND transport duty. Children’s social care: +£3bn to councils; extended staying put; access to counselling.

Housing and planning
- Build 150,000 new social homes/yr; end Right to Buy. Rent controls via local authorities; end no‑fault evictions; new long-term tenancies and tenancy boards. Retrofit and standards: new homes to Passivhaus-equivalent with solar and low‑carbon heat; raise PRS minimum to EPC C. Retrofit programme over five years: £29bn homes (to EPC B), £4bn public buildings, £9bn low‑carbon heating, £7bn overheating adaptation. Bring empty homes into use; first-refusal powers for councils on specified properties. Whole-life carbon in planning; reuse of demolition materials; protect Green Belt; ensure developments are not car-dependent.

Energy and climate
- No new oil/gas licences; end subsidies; carbon tax rising over a decade (indicative path up to £500/t). Expand renewables: target by 2035 of 80GW offshore wind, 53GW onshore, 100GW solar; aim for wind to supply ~70% of electricity by 2030; end onshore wind barriers; rooftop solar on new homes. Community ownership thresholds for projects; Crown Estate into public ownership (Welsh assets devolved). Grid expansion, interconnectors, storage, green hydrogen. End imported biomass subsidies. No new nuclear; phase out existing stations.

Economy, investment and industry
- Green investment averaging £40bn/yr in parliament (electricity, retrofit/heat/adaptation, rail, public transport, active travel, industry decarbonisation, water/sewage, utility buyouts). R&D +£30bn over five years. Public ownership of rail, water, and Big 5 retail energy suppliers. Finance: BoE mandate to include transition; credit guidance; fossil divestment by 2030 across licensed banks and major non-banks; FCA to phase out fossil equities. Regional mutual banks (UKIB plus £10bn), £2bn/yr local decarbonisation grants. Circular economy/repair and product standards.

Work and incomes
- Repeal recent anti‑union laws; Charter of Workers’ Rights; day‑one rights; platform workers classed as “workers”. Minimum wage £15/hr (offset for small firms via higher Employment Allowance). 10:1 pay ratio cap for organisations. Equal pay audits; safe sick pay; progress toward shorter working week.

Welfare and tax
- Universal Credit and legacy benefits +£40/week; end five‑week wait; scrap two‑child cap; carers allowance +10%/month; maintain pension uprating; end sanctions; long‑term goal of UBI.
- Tax: Wealth tax 1% >£10m and 2% >£1bn; align CGT and investment income with earnings; remove NI upper limit; standardise pension tax relief at basic rate; reform inheritance tax; Council Tax revaluation; remove selected business rate reliefs; windfall taxes (oil/gas, banks); VAT cuts (hospitality/arts) and rises (financial services/private education); carbon tax introduction. Stronger anti‑avoidance; borrowing to invest subject to inflation risk.

Nature, animals, food
- Rights of Nature Act; 30% land/sea protected by 2030; DEFRA +£1.5bn; water companies to public ownership; Clean Air Act; Right to Roam. Peat rewetting; woodland increase; urban biodiversity measures; ban destructive fishing in MPAs.
- Animal measures: Commission on Animal Protection; ban blood sports; licensing and cruelty register; phase out factory farming practices; ban lead ammo/snaring; reduce animal testing.
- Food/farming: Nearly triple farm support; link payments to pesticide reduction; shift to mixed farming, more horticulture; free school meals for all and breakfast clubs; food education; strengthen GCA/FSA; expand productive forestry and wood recycling.

Education
- Scrap tuition fees; restore maintenance grants; long‑term address graduate debt. Schools: +£8bn incl. £2bn for teacher pay; £2.5bn/yr for buildings/RAAC; broaden curriculum; Natural History GCSE; RSHE retained. Move academies/free schools to LA control; VAT on private school fees (SEND exempt). SEND: +£5bn; school nurses and counsellors. Early years: £1.4bn/yr for Sure Start; 35 hrs childcare from 9 months. FE: +£3bn sixth form; £12bn lifelong learning; restore EMA.

Transport
- Rail/bus subsidies to £10bn/yr by end of parliament; £19bn/5yrs for public transport, electrification, walking/cycling; £2.5bn/yr active travel; nationalise rail; local control of buses. Restore fuel duty escalator; road pricing; oppose new roads. EV transition: scrappage up to £5bn/yr; end new ICE sales by 2027 and road use by 2035; weight‑based VED; 20mph default in built-up areas; shift freight to rail. Aviation: frequent‑flyer levy; ban domestic flights with <3h rail alternative; no airport expansion; tax kerosene via carbon tax.

Democracy, rights, migration, digital
- Fair Politics Act: repeal Elections Act 2022; PR for elections; party state funding; stronger lobbying/think‑tank transparency; votes at 16; Online Safety Act amendments. Replace Lords with elected chamber; devolution enhancements; defend HRA/ECHR; restore legal aid; repeal recent protest laws; self‑ID for trans people, end spousal veto, X passport option.
- Migration: end hostile environment; remove Minimum Income Requirement; safe asylum routes; right to work for asylum seekers; abolish NRPF and 10‑year route; limit detention; residence‑based voting; split Home Office functions; cost‑price visas; NHS access; broaden family reunion.
- Arts/media/digital: £5bn/5yrs for local arts/sport/culture; VAT exemption for cultural events; media ownership caps; implement Leveson; local media grants; Digital Bill of Rights; precautionary AI regulation aligned with EU/UNESCO; protect creators’ IP and workers’ rights.

Justice and drugs
- End routine stop/search and facial recognition; improve police accountability/training. Presumption against sentences <2 years; diversion schemes. Strategy and funding to tackle violence against women/girls; decriminalise sex work. MoJ +£11bn over parliament to fix courts/legal aid. National commission on drug law; decriminalise personal possession; harm‑reduction approach.

Foreign policy and defence
- Support Ukraine; strengthen international law; remove ISDS in trade deals. EU: pursue re‑entry (customs union first), restore free movement and Erasmus. Aid to 1% GNI by 2033; climate finance to 1.5% GNI incl. Loss & Damage; debt relief; support ecocide law and Global South leadership. Nuclear: sign TPNW, cancel Trident, dismantle arsenal. NATO: remain, advocate no‑first‑use and defensive focus.

Fiscal outline (selected)
- Additional revenues targeted from personal/wealth taxes, business taxes and carbon taxes; borrowing to invest, with inflation as primary constraint. Estimated added tax revenue by end of parliament: personal/wealth £50–70bn/yr; carbon up to ~£80bn/yr; business up to £40bn over five years. Additional capital and revenue spending rises across health, social care, education, transport, nature, and overseas aid.

Judge whether A or B aligns more closely with this profile, taking into account that each foundation may be invoked in either direction.

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else. Do not wrap it in markdown code fences and do not add commentary before or after it. The object must have exactly these keys, in this order:

{
  "evidence": "<the specific commitments in each text you relied on>",
  "reasoning": "<two sentences connecting that evidence to the verdict>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "winner": "A" | "B"
}
